title: VPC Topology Guardian: Terraform module for private deployments with proactive health probes and upgrade hooks
creator: Maya Tran
description:
Build a production-ready Terraform module that standardizes VPC topology for Redwood Private deployments and includes automated health probes and upgrade hooks. The module (vpc-topology-guardian) should cover multi-AZ subnet provisioning (public, private with NAT, isolated), optional IGW vs managed NAT Gateways, configurable VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, Secrets Manager, STS, CloudWatch Logs), route tables per AZ, and tagging/iam metadata conventions required for auditability.

Key design goals: minimize blast radius during upgrades, surface clear health signals for networking primitives, support multi-account/landing-zone patterns, and be easy to consume by both the Private control plane and customer IaC. Module should be provider-agnostic where possible (AWS focus first) and include opinionated defaults plus overrides for advanced users.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exists in infra-terraform/modules/vpc-topology-guardian with versioned releases (v0.1.0 initial)
Module supports creating public, private (NAT) and isolated subnets spread across N AZs from a single input variable
Configurable NAT strategy: internet_gateway + egress_cidr OR managed NAT gateways with autoscaling recommendation notes
VPC endpoints created for required services when enabled and validated by integration tests
Route tables are generated per subnet class and include tags that map to Redwood telemetry (team, environment, provisioned_by)

Health checks implemented: automated periodic endpoint validation, NAT gateway reachability tests, and route-table sanity checks that report to a CloudWatch/Stackdriver metric and Redwood Console dashboard
Module exposes lifecycle hooks: pre-upgrade validation plan, canary subnet upgrade workflow, and post-upgrade smoke test job definitions
Terratest and GitHub Actions run integration tests that create a small ephemeral VPC, exercise endpoints and NAT paths, and run smoke traffic against an internal canary service
Documentation and example usage: single-account and multi-account references, upgrade playbook, and failure-mode remediation steps

implementation_notes: Use module inputs to drive AZ count, subnet CIDR / per-AZ sizing, and enable/disable lists for endpoints
Provide a single 'nat_strategy' variable with options ['managed_nat','eip_nat','egress_only_igw'] and clear docs for trade-offs
Create a 'health_probe' submodule that spins up minimal lambda/k8s job to run endpoint simulations and write metrics to a dedicated namespace
Expose outputs for peering attachment IDs, route table IDs, and endpoint IDs to be consumed by downstream modules (eg: bastion, vpn)
Keep resource naming deterministic and make names overridable via a 'name_prefix' variable
Pin terraform provider versions in examples and add upgrade notes for AWS provider v4 -> v5 migration paths
Add a migration script and checklist for existing customers using previous vpc modules to move to guardian with minimal downtime
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Accidental deletion/recreation of NAT gateways during upgrades can cause traffic blackholes — Mitigation: add lifecycle.prevent_destroy on critical resources and a canary upgrade path
Risk: Endpoint policy misconfiguration could expose secrets — Mitigation: include secure-by-default example policies and require security_review_required for any policy overrides
Risk: Multi-account dependency complexity — Mitigation: provide example patterns for centralized endpoints vs per-account endpoints and test both in CI
